Direct Known Subclasses:
DemoMapView
public class MapView2D extends BaseView
A two-dimensional map view that renders world maps using configurable projections and themes.

Responsibilities

  • Managing the active IMapProjection and the world coordinate system exposed to the IContainer.
  • Orchestrating the rendering pipeline (background → ocean → graticule → countries → cities) via an after-draw IDrawable.
  • Providing per-frame feedback strings (projection name, lat/lon, picked country and city) to the FeedbackPane.
  • Exposing public API (setProjection(EProjection), getCityRenderer(), etc.) so MapControlPanel can drive changes without accessing private state.

Shared vs. per-view data

Country and city data were previously stored in static fields, which created a hidden singleton: all MapView2D instances shared — and could inadvertently overwrite — the same dataset. The fields are now instance fields so that multiple views can independently hold different datasets. The static setter methods (setCountries(List), setCities(List)) are retained for backwards compatibility; they set the data on the most-recently-constructed instance through a static reference that is updated in the constructor. Callers that only ever create one view are unaffected.

Side panel layout

The control panel (MapControlPanel) and feedback pane (FeedbackPane) are placed together in a combined east-side strip whose preferred width in pixels is controlled by getSidePanelWidth().

  • Constructor Details

    • MapView2D

      public MapView2D(Object... keyVals)
      Creates a map view. Variable-length keyVals are passed through to BaseView for framework-level configuration (title, toolbar flags, container factory, etc.).

      The view initializes with the MapConstants.DEFAULT_PROJECTION and a light MapTheme. Geographic data (setCountries(List), setCities(List)) must be loaded and set before the first render to avoid a blank map.

      Parameters:
      keyVals - framework key-value pairs forwarded to BaseView

    • getSidePanelWidth

      protected int getSidePanelWidth()
      Gets the preferred width of the east-side strip containing the map control panel, custom application panels, and feedback pane.

      Subclasses may override this to request a wider or narrower side panel. The override should not depend on subclass instance fields, because this method is called during MapView2D construction before the subclass constructor body has run. Returning a literal or subclass static constant is safe.

      Returns:
      preferred side-panel width in pixels

    • getElevation

      public double getElevation(double lat, double lon)
      Returns interpolated elevation or bathymetry at a geographic location.

      Elevation remains available even when the ETOPO5 layer is hidden. Layer visibility is a presentation choice and should not affect calculations such as radar line-of-sight or land-height feedback.

      Parameters:
      lat - latitude in degrees
      lon - longitude in degrees
      Returns:
      elevation in metres, or NaN if ETOPO5 is not installed or either coordinate is non-finite

    • setProjection

      public void setProjection(EProjection projectionType)
      Switches the active projection to one of MDI's built-in projection types, rebuilding all dependent renderers and resetting the container's world coordinate system.

      The new projection is created by ProjectionFactory using the theme currently selected in the control panel, so the visual style is preserved across projection changes.

      Country and city data must have been set (via setCountries(List) and setCities(List)) before calling this method; if either list is null the corresponding renderer is skipped.

      This method preserves the existing MDI enum-based projection API. For application-supplied projections, use setProjection(IMapProjection).

      Parameters:
      projectionType - the new built-in projection type; must not be null

    • addShapefile

      public void addShapefile(ShapeFeatureRenderer renderer)
      Appends a ShapeFeatureRenderer to the end of the extra-layer list. Extra layers are drawn after country polygons and before city markers, in the order they were added.

      Typical use: 

      List<ShapeFeature> rivers = new ShapefileFeatureLoader().load(Path.of("ne_10m_rivers_lake_centerlines.shp"));
ShapeFeatureStyle style = new ShapeFeatureStyle().strokeColor(new Color(0x6B9FD4)).strokeWidth(0.8f);
mapView.addLayer(new ShapeFeatureRenderer(rivers, mapView.getProjection(), style));
      Parameters:
      renderer - the layer to add; must not be null

    • loadShapefileLayer

      public static List<ShapeFeature> loadShapefileLayer(MapView2D mapView, Path path, String name, ShapeFeatureStyle style)
      Convenience method that loads a shapefile from the given path, creates a ShapeFeatureRenderer with the specified style, and adds it as a new layer with the given name.

      Exceptions are caught and logged to the console; the method does not throw.

      Parameters:
      mapView - the view to add the layer to; must not be null
      path - filesystem path to the shapefile; must not be null
      name - display name shown in the Shapefiles menu; must not be null
      style - rendering style for the shapefile features; must not be null

      public void drawSymbol(Graphics2D g, double lat, double lon, SymbolType type, int size, Color lineColor, Color fillColor)
      Draws a map symbol at the given latitude and longitude using the active projection to convert to screen coordinates.

      Used by MapControlPanel to draw the projection center marker. Can also be used by application code to draw symbols on top of the map without managing coordinate transforms.

      Parameters:
      g - graphics context to draw on; must not be null
      lat - latitude in degrees; must be between -90 and 90
      lon - longitude in degrees; must be between -180 and 180
      type - symbol type; must not be null
      size - symbol size in pixels; must be positive
      lineColor - color for symbol outlines and lines; must not be null
      fillColor - color for symbol fills; must not be null

    • getFeedbackStrings

      public void getFeedbackStrings(IContainer container, Point pp, Point2D.Double wp, List<String> feedbackStrings)
      Default feedback implementation: no-op. Subclasses override to provide coordinate or status strings.

      Appends the following strings (in order) to feedbackStrings:

      1. Number of countries loaded.
      2. Number of cities loaded.
      3. Active projection name.
      4. Screen coordinates of the cursor.
      5. World (projection-space) coordinates.
      6. Latitude and longitude in degrees (only when cursor is on map).
      7. Picked country name and ISO code (only when cursor is on a country polygon).
      8. Styled feedback text from any extra layers (ShapeFeatureRenderer) whose IPickable.pick(Point, IContainer) returns a non-null result. Each layer contributes at most one string; all hit layers are reported.
      9. Picked city name and population (only when cursor is near a city dot).
      Specified by:
      getFeedbackStrings in interface IFeedbackProvider
      Overrides:
      getFeedbackStrings in class BaseView
      Parameters:
      container - the container.
      pp - the mouse location.
      wp - the corresponding world point.
      feedbackStrings - the List of feedback strings to add to.

      protected void drawCustomMapContent(Graphics2D g2, IContainer container)
      Placeholder method for subclasses to override and draw custom map content after the standard layers. Not called by default since most views won't need it, but available for extensibility when needed.

      This is not registered as an after-draw IDrawable since that would require a separate registration and coordinate transform for each subclass; instead, subclasses can call this method directly from their own after-draw implementation after calling super.drawCustomMapContent(g2).

    • setProjection

      public void setProjection(IMapProjection newProjection)
      Switches the active projection to an application-supplied projection.

      This is the extensibility path for projections that are not represented by EProjection. The supplied projection must be fully initialized, including its MapTheme. The view rebuilds its graticule, country, city, and extra-layer renderers and resets the world coordinate system using the projection's own IMapProjection.getXYBounds().

      Parameters:
      newProjection - the new projection; must not be null

    • hoverUpdate

      public void hoverUpdate(HoverEvent he)
      Handle a hover event.

      Subclasses can override this method to respond to hover events, which are triggered by mouse movement with no buttons down. The default implementation is a no-op.

      When the user hovers over the map, this method displays a small window with the country name and any configured shapefile feedback fields found under the cursor. The information is shown in the HoverInfoWindow provided by the MapContainer.

      Overrides:
      hoverUpdate in class BaseView
      Parameters:
